title: UAP Adviser Urges US to Add Context to Released UFO Files
excerpt: Psychologist Jennice Vilhauer urges the US government to provide investigative context for UFO files and confirms officials have planned for a possible confirmation of nonhuman intelligence.

Public access to government records about unidentified anomalous phenomena could do more to clarify unexplained sightings if officials provided additional investigative details, psychologist Jennice Vilhauer said. In an October 13, 2026, report by FemaleFirst, Vilhauer urged the US government to explain how individual cases were examined, what evidence investigators considered and why some incidents remain unresolved.

Vilhauer serves on the advisory board of the Disclosure Foundation and President Donald Trump's Scientific Advisory Council on UAP. She supports releasing military records but argues that documents without sufficient context can leave the public unable to assess the evidence or distinguish established findings from speculation.

In a Substack post, Vilhauer criticized the limited explanatory information available through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, known as PURSUE.

"Although the PURSUE [ Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters] website provides some general context and explains that the materials represent unresolved cases, it provides very little information for understanding individual files or incidents. Without that information, there is no real way to tell what is being seen and people are left to come up with their own explanations. This kind of situation creates the perfect scenario for misinformation to fill the gaps and existing views to become even more polarized.

Those who are inclined to believe the objects are signs of non-human intelligence (NHI) will argue that they provide proof, while skeptics will continue to believe there is nothing worth seeing. People in the middle are likely to become more confused or simply grow bored and disengage." Vilhauer wrote.

She argued that additional explanations could improve public understanding without requiring officials to disclose every sensitive detail. She also said that the government could explain investigative limitations and identify information that was never collected or remains withheld, allowing experts and the public to assess the available evidence more carefully.

Vilhauer expanded on that argument in her discussion of what meaningful disclosure should include.

"If scientists can’t make sense of what is being released, what good is the data doing the average person? Don’t get me wrong, I wholeheartedly support these releases and want to see more, but transparency without context isn’t really transparency. At minimum, each file should provide enough context to explain what analysis or investigation was conducted, what prevented investigators from reaching a conclusion.

If there is missing data, it should be clear whether it was never collected or why it is being withheld ... Explanations reduce anxiety even when they do not provide certainty. It doesn’t require revealing every detail.

The general public understands the need to protect national security. Providing context also wouldn’t mean the government is telling the public what to believe. It would simply allow people to evaluate the material more accurately."

Vilhauer wrote.

Her call for clearer documentation follows a separate disclosure about US preparations for the possibility of confirming nonhuman intelligence. In a Substack post published October 9, 2026, Vilhauer said council members had been informed that the government maintained a preparedness plan for such a scenario.

Vilhauer said the information was shared at a meeting of the UAP Science Advisory Council at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence on August 31, 2026. She stressed that the existence of a contingency plan does not establish that officials have confirmed extraterrestrial life.

"At a meeting held on August 31, 2026, at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the UAP Science Advisory Council, of which I am a member, was informed that the United States government has a preparedness plan in place should the existence of nonhuman intelligence (NHI) be confirmed. We were also told that the United States is prepared to take an international leadership role if necessary." Vilhauer wrote.

She described the planning as evidence that officials had considered the potential consequences of such a confirmation, while emphasizing that council members had not received details about how the government would respond.

"The existence of a preparedness plan ... does mean that the possibility of confirming NHI [non-human intelligence] has been taken seriously enough to warrant advance planning. That alone is significant because it means that the United States government has considered the possibility that such a confirmation could occur and it has determined that the consequences would be substantial enough to require a coordinated response." Vilhauer wrote.

According to Vilhauer, officials did not identify the agencies that would lead a response, explain the circumstances that might activate the plan or clarify whether it addressed the psychological and societal effects of a confirmation.

"We were not given any details about the plan. We do not know which agencies would lead the response, what circumstances would activate it, or whether it addresses the psychological and societal impact of such information. Those questions matter because preparing to release information is not the same as preparing people to understand and adapt to it." Vilhauer wrote.
